links.outcome: Checklist coverage variation across chatbot configurations and clinical presentations
links.effect: Coverage varied by configuration (DT 72.3% vs MN 54.0%) and by symptom (palpitations 77.6% vs nausea and vomiting 46.07%); repeated questions in 4-15% of transcripts depending on mode.
links.quote: Repetitive questioning was uncommon overall but occurred more often in nonthinking configurations than in thinking configurations, most frequently in the MN configuration.

links.outcome: History coverage of LLM chatbot configurations versus rule-based baseline on same cases
links.effect: DT coverage 72.3% vs choice baseline 51.1% (Hedge g 1.53, P<.001); MN did not differ significantly from choice (P>.99).
links.quote: Post hoc pairwise t tests with Bonferroni correction ( Table 2 ) showed that the DT mode significantly outperformed all other configurations.

links.effect: Prompt detail was significant: F1,65=56.74; P<.001; η²G=0.085; DT mean coverage 72.3% vs MN 54.0%.
links.quote: This analysis showed significant main effects of prompt detail ( F 1, 65 =56.74; P <.001; η² G =0.085) and internal reasoning ( F 1, 65 =47.45; P <.001; η² G =0.096).

links.effect: Lowest symptom coverage: nausea/vomiting 46.07% (SD 6.34%), impaired vision 46.11% (SD 5.76%), fever 47.79% (SD 9.13%).
links.quote: In contrast, the lowest-coverage symptoms were nausea and vomiting (46.07%, SD 6.34%), impaired vision (46.11%, SD 5.76%), and fever (47.79%, SD 9.13%).

links.effect: DT outperformed Choice (t65=9.71; P<.001; g=1.53), but MN and Choice did not differ (t65=1.48; P>.99).
links.quote: The MN and choice modes did not differ significantly ( P >.99).

links.effect: Detailed prompt significantly improved coverage (F=56.74, P<.001); detailed prompt with thinking achieved 72.3% mean coverage vs 60.5% for minimal prompt with thinking, 59.8% for detailed nonthinking, and 54.0% for minimal nonthinking.
links.quote: Overall, these findings demonstrate that both prompt detail and internal reasoning are associated with improved information completeness, with their combination in the DT mode producing the greatest coverage.
